questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why electric cars are too expensive for most people
How car companies in the US and China compete for customers
How electric scooters and rickshaws in India help fight pollution
Why India wants to build more metro lines
questions.why: They discuss the growing role of electric vehicles, especially two- and three-wheelers in India.

questions.q: What is Neil's opinion of electric cars?
options: They are dangerous to drive
They are a good idea, but few people can afford them
They are actually worse for the planet than petrol or diesel cars
He would buy one tomorrow
questions.why: He says they're great in theory, “but who has the money to buy one?!”

questions.q: How many two- and three-wheelers in India are now electric?
options: About 10%
About a quarter
Almost none
More than half
questions.why: Neil says over half of these vehicles are now electric.

questions.q: Why is there some debate about how green EVs are in India?
options: Most of India's electricity still comes from coal
The batteries are all made in other countries and shipped in
Electric scooters break down very often
EVs use more energy than petrol cars
questions.why: Beth says more than three quarters of India's electricity is still generated by coal.

questions.q: According to Louise Ribet, what one word explains why two- and three-wheelers are popular?
options: Speed
Convenience
Fashion
Better safety
questions.why: She says it can be summarised in one word: convenience.

questions.q: Why did two- and three-wheelers spread in Indian cities, according to Ribet?
options: Public transport there isn't good or frequent enough
The government gave them away for free
Cars were banned from city centres
People copied the transport systems of London and Singapore
questions.why: She says they spread because of a lack of good, frequent public transport.

questions.q: What does Graihagh Jackson suggest about closing schools because of smog?
options: It is the best way to protect children
It should happen more often
It doesn't really fix the problem
It only happens in summer
questions.why: She says, “that's hardly a solution is it!”

questions.q: What is the Indian government's target for 2030?
options: To ban all petrol scooters
To make every rickshaw electric
To build lots of new metro lines across Delhi
To have 30% of vehicles on the road electric
questions.why: Graihagh says by 2030 the government wants 30% of vehicles on the road to be electric.
